results.name: single_shared_factor_nonmultiple_contrast
results.description: In single-example sets, yes-rate for targets that share a common factor >=3 with the example but are neither its multiple nor its divisor (e.g. 12 after "15", 9 after "6", 27 after "30"), minus yes-rate for targets with gcd(target, example) < 3 that are not multiples/divisors; observed > null means people generalize to factor-kin of a lone example beyond pure multiples, which the model (multiples route only) under-produces.
results.code:
# name: single_shared_factor_nonmultiple_contrast
# description: In single-example sets, yes-rate for targets that share a common factor >=3 with the example but are neither its multiple nor its divisor (e.g. 12 after "15", 9 after "6", 27 after "30"), minus yes-rate for targets with gcd(target, example) < 3 that are not multiples/divisors; observed > null means people generalize to factor-kin of a lone example beyond pure multiples, which the model (multiples route only) under-produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",").to_numpy()
    e = pd.to_numeric(s.str.split(",").str[0], errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    e = np.where(np.isnan(e) | (e < 1), 1.0, e).astype(np.int64)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(np.int64)
    g = np.gcd(t, e)
    mult = (t % e == 0)
    div = (e % t == 0)
    kin = (g >= 3) & ~mult & ~div
    other = (g < 3) & ~mult & ~div
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a, b = single & kin, single & other
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: multiple_route_example_size_contrast
results.description: Among targets >=10 from every example and sharing no example's final digit, yes-rate for targets that are multiples of a two-digit example (>=10, e.g. 94 after 47, 62 after 31) minus yes-rate for targets that are multiples only of a one-digit example (2-9, e.g. 49 after 7); observed > null means multiples of large examples are endorsed relatively more than the model's size-independent route predicts, observed < null means the route is really driven by small examples (times-table knowledge).
results.code:
# name: multiple_route_example_size_contrast
# description: Among targets >=10 from every example and sharing no example's final digit, yes-rate for targets that are multiples of a two-digit example (>=10, e.g. 94 after 47, 62 after 31) minus yes-rate for targets that are multiples only of a one-digit example (2-9, e.g. 49 after 7); observed > null means multiples of large examples are endorsed relatively more than the model's size-independent route predicts, observed < null means the route is really driven by small examples (times-table knowledge).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)[:, None]
    pres = ~np.isnan(ex)
    e = np.where(pres, ex, 1e9)
    e1 = np.where(pres, ex, 1.0)
    far = (np.abs(t - e) >= 10).all(1)
    nodig = ~((np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(e, 10)) & pres).any(1)
    m = pres & (e > 1) & (np.mod(t, e1) == 0) & (t != e)
    big = (m & (e >= 10)).any(1)
    small = (m & (e < 10)).any(1)
    base = far & nodig
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a, b = base & big, base & small & ~big
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: interior_vs_exterior_contrast
results.description: In sets with >=2 examples, among targets 4-20 from the nearest example that share no example's final digit and are not multiples of any example, yes-rate for targets strictly inside the examples' range minus targets outside it; observed > null means people fill in the interval spanned by the examples (range/hull generalization) more than summed exemplar similarity predicts, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: interior_vs_exterior_contrast
# description: In sets with >=2 examples, among targets 4-20 from the nearest example that share no example's final digit and are not multiples of any example, yes-rate for targets strictly inside the examples' range minus targets outside it; observed > null means people fill in the interval spanned by the examples (range/hull generalization) more than summed exemplar similarity predicts, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t1 = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    t = t1[:, None]
    pres = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = pres.sum(1)
    e = np.where(pres, ex, 1e9)
    e1 = np.where(pres, ex, 1.0)
    d = np.abs(t - e).min(1)
    nodig = ~((np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(e, 10)) & pres).any(1)
    mult = (pres & (e > 1) & (np.mod(t, e1) == 0) & (t != e)).any(1)
    lo = np.nanmin(np.where(pres, ex, np.inf), axis=1)
    hi = np.nanmax(np.where(pres, ex, -np.inf), axis=1)
    inside = (t1 > lo) & (t1 < hi)
    base = (n >= 2) & (d >= 4) & (d <= 20) & nodig & ~mult
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a, b = base & inside, base & ~inside
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: item_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation, across distinct (set, target) items, of each item's yes-rate; observed > null means items are more polarized (people agree more strongly on clear yes / clear no items) than the model's item probabilities produce, i.e. the model under-discriminates between items; observed < null means it over-discriminates.

results.name: small_vs_large_magnitude_near_contrast
results.description: Among targets 3-15 from their nearest example, sharing no example's final digit and not multiples of any example, yes-rate when that nearest example is <=30 minus when it is >=60; observed < null means a given numeric distance counts as more dissimilar among small numbers (log/Weber-compressed magnitude) than the model's linear distance predicts, observed > null means the opposite.
results.code:
# name: small_vs_large_magnitude_near_contrast
# description: Among targets 3-15 from their nearest example, sharing no example's final digit and not multiples of any example, yes-rate when that nearest example is <=30 minus when it is >=60; observed < null means a given numeric distance counts as more dissimilar among small numbers (log/Weber-compressed magnitude) than the model's linear distance predicts, observed > null means the opposite.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)[:, None]
    pres = ~np.isnan(ex)
    e = np.where(pres, ex, 1e9)
    e1 = np.where(pres, ex, 1.0)
    D = np.abs(t - e)
    j = np.argmin(D, axis=1)
    d = D[np.arange(len(j)), j]
    near_ex = e[np.arange(len(j)), j]
    nodig = ~((np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(e, 10)) & pres).any(1)
    mult = (pres & (e > 1) & (np.mod(t, e1) == 0) & (t != e)).any(1)
    base = (d >= 3) & (d <= 15) & nodig & ~mult
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a, b = base & (near_ex <= 30), base & (near_ex >= 60)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: above_vs_below_range_contrast
results.description: Among targets outside the examples' range, 5-30 from the nearest example, sharing no example's final digit and not a multiple of any example, yes-rate for targets above the largest example minus targets below the smallest; observed > null means people extend the set upward more than downward (directional generalization) beyond the model's symmetric magnitude similarity, observed < null means downward extension is favoured.

results.name: multiset_far_multiple_contrast
results.description: In sets with >=2 examples, yes-rate for targets that are a multiple (not equal) of some example >1 yet >=10 from every example and sharing no example's final digit, minus yes-rate for equally far non-matching non-multiple targets; observed > null means people use the multiples route in multi-example sets more than the model's fixed additive route predicts, observed < null means the model over-credits multiples once several examples are shown.
results.code:
# name: multiset_far_multiple_contrast
# description: In sets with >=2 examples, yes-rate for targets that are a multiple (not equal) of some example >1 yet >=10 from every example and sharing no example's final digit, minus yes-rate for equally far non-matching non-multiple targets; observed > null means people use the multiples route in multi-example sets more than the model's fixed additive route predicts, observed < null means the model over-credits multiples once several examples are shown.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)[:, None]
    pres = ~np.isnan(ex)
    e = np.where(pres, ex, 1e9)
    n = pres.sum(1)
    far = (np.abs(t - e) >= 10).all(1)
    nodig = ~((np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(e, 10)) & pres).any(1)
    mult = (pres & (e > 1) & (np.mod(t, np.where(pres, ex, 1.0)) == 0) & (t != e)).any(1)
    base = (n >= 2) & far & nodig
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a, b = base & mult, base & ~mult
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: divisor_of_example_contrast
results.description: Yes-rate for targets (>=2) that are a proper divisor of some example (e.g. 7 after 49, 8 after 64), are >=5 from every example and share no example's final digit, minus yes-rate for other such far non-matching targets that neither divide nor are multiples of any example; observed > null means people generalize downward to factors of an example (a 'divisor route' the model lacks), observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: divisor_of_example_contrast
# description: Yes-rate for targets (>=2) that are a proper divisor of some example (e.g. 7 after 49, 8 after 64), are >=5 from every example and share no example's final digit, minus yes-rate for other such far non-matching targets that neither divide nor are multiples of any example; observed > null means people generalize downward to factors of an example (a 'divisor route' the model lacks), observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)[:, None]
    pres = ~np.isnan(ex)
    e = np.where(pres, ex, 1e9)
    e1 = np.where(pres, ex, 1.0)
    far = (np.abs(t - e) >= 5).all(1)
    nodig = ~((np.mod(t, 10) == np.mod(e, 10)) & pres).any(1)
    div = (pres & (t >= 2) & (t < e) & (np.mod(e1, t) == 0)).any(1)
    mult = (pres & (e > 1) & (np.mod(t, e1) == 0) & (t != e)).any(1)
    base = far & nodig
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    a, b = base & div, base & ~div & ~mult
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
